report:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Transformación quística parcial del tercio proximal del LCA. LCP y ligamentos colaterales dentro de límites
normales.
Aumento de señal central del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial que contacta la superficie
articular inferior sugieran una rotura.
Rotura del cuerno anterior, cuerpo y cuerno posterior del menisco lateral con mínima extrusión. Esto se
asocia a edema las partes blandas regionales.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y total de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral
medial. Úlceras condrales espesor parcial de la región central del platillo tibial lateral. Condropatía
superficial del resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral.
Úlceras condrales de espesor total de distribución difusa de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular con discreta sinovitis. No hay quistes poplíteos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de
límites normales.
Impresión:
Signos de una rotura del menisco medial, no desplazada.
Rotura compleja del cuerno anterior, cuerpo y cuerno posterior del menisco lateral con mínima extrusión y
edema de las partes blandas regionales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 3 de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial y del
platillo tibial lateral.
Condropatía superficial del resto de los compartimentos femorotibiales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 y 3 de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular con discreta sinovitis difusa.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. Large complex popliteal cyst measuring up to 65 mm with an 11 mm osseous body in the superior aspect of the cyst. Sliver of free fluid along the inferior margin of the popliteal cyst suggesting minimal recent partial rupture.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Moderate degenerative change.
Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal horizontal oblique component of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with inferior surfacing. Fraying and blunting of the meniscal free edge.
Mild thickening of the proximal MCL compatible with remote injury.
Diffuse low grade partial-thickness chondral loss. Marginal osteophytosis.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Severe degenerative change with full-thickness chondral loss of the weightbearing and posterior portion of the compartment, with subchondral reactive marrow change. Marginal osteophytosis.
Complex degenerative multidirectional tear of the posterior horn extending into the body with significant maceration and substance loss of the body and anterior and posterior horn with minimal residual meniscal substance. There is some extrusion of the body of the lateral meniscus.
Thickened popliteus insertion with intrasubstance signal compatible with moderate tendinosis
Mildly thickened lateral collateral ligament proper which could reflect the sequela of a remote injury. Mild distal biceps tendinosis.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Degenerative changes of the anterior cruciate ligament which remains intact. The PCL is intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Mild chondropathy. Small marginal osteophytes. Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis. Mild edema at the suprapatellar fat pad.
Scarring at that the Hoffa's fat pad which could reflect the previous surgery-for clinical correlation.

Bones:
See above.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
The intra-articular body is seen at the suprapatellar joint recess on the previous MRI is no longer present.

CONCLUSION:
1.Interval worsening of the severe osteoarthritis of the lateral compartment. Complex degenerative tearing and extensive maceration the lateral meniscus.
2.Moderate degenerative change of the medial compartment. Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal oblique tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus.
3.Mild degenerative change of the patellofemoral compartment.
4.Large complex popliteal cyst with an osseous body.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multisequence multiplanar MRI of the left knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Meniscus injury?

COMPARISON:  Radiographs of bilateral knees [Date].

FINDINGS:
There is a 5 mm intermediate signal particle along the medial aspect of the medial femoral condyle, deep to the medial collateral ligament. This was present as a small mineralized focus on the prior radiographs from <[Month]> <[YEAR]>, stable in size. No adjacent soft tissue or bone marrow edema.

The cruciate and collateral ligaments are intact. Minimal thickening of the medial collateral ligament proximally is suggestive of remote low-grade injury/sprain. Posterolateral corner supporting structures of the knee are intact.

There is an oblique radial/parrot beak tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. No displaced flap fragment. No parameniscal cyst. Borderline extrusion of the medial meniscus mid body.

The lateral meniscus is intact.

There is a full-thickness chondral defect over the central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle, measuring approximately 1.6 x 1.0 cm (AP x ML). No subchondral marrow edema or fracture. Articular cartilage is otherwise well-maintained in the lateral tibiofemoral and patellofemoral compartments.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

Moderate joint effusion. No synovitis. Small Baker's cyst, without evidence of cystic compression/rupture.


INTERPRETATION:
 Oblique radial tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
Full-thickness chondral defect over the central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle without subchondral marrow edema.

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Severe edema of the medial condyle of left knee.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
Prior MRI dated <[Date]> of <[Month]> <[YEAR]>

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intra since degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface. Findings are ready seen on prior study but appears more degenerate. Several para meniscal cysts are seen at the posterior aspect of the meniscus measuring up to 0.4 cm in size. Meniscal extrusion approximately 0.6 cm noted.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. Trace Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: A large subchondral cysts are seen at the posterior superior aspect of the tibial plateau, very much larger than prior study. Moderate degenerative changes multiple osteophytes are seen, most significant at the medial tibiofemoral joint. No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Minimal chondrosis..

Medial compartment: Focal full-thickness chondral loss measuring up to 1.3 cm in size associated subchondral edema. Moderate chondrosis in the rest of the femoral condyle Findings have slightly progressed compared to prior study.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondral irregularity. No significant subchondral edema.

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface, similar to previous. Interval increase in degenerative changes of the meniscus is observed. Meniscal extrusion of approximately 0.6 cm is seen. Multiple para meniscal cysts are also present.

Interval increase in degenerative changes are identified evident as shown by increased osteophytes, full-thickness chondral loss at the medial tibiofemoral joint associated increasing subchondral edema, and multiple enlarging subchondral cysts at the posterior medial tibial plateau.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left medial knee pain after tripping and striking left knee on a box at work.  History of RA. 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.  

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: 
Marked marrow edema in the lateral tibial plateau. Alignment is anatomic.  No aggressive osseous lesions.  

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Radial oblique tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with mild extrusion. 6 x 3 mm parameniscal cyst at the posterior horn, body junction. 
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade cartilage loss, weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. 8 x 5 mm full-thickness cartilage defect posterior weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. High grade partial thickness cartilage loss of the tibial plateau. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.  
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade cartilage fraying spanning the lateral compartment. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: 
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Mild heterogeneity of the patellar cartilage.     

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.  
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.  

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.  
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. 

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear. 
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear. 
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.  
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad.  No lateral patellar tilt or translation.  No patella alta.  Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm. 

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy.  Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact. 

SOFT TISSUES:
Edema identified in the medial subcutaneous fat. 
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. 

IMPRESSION:
1.	Intense marrow edema in the medial tibial plateau. Findings may reflect contusion or severe osseous stress response/developing stress fracture.
2.	Radial oblique tear of the medial meniscus with mild extrusion.
3.	High-grade medial compartment chondrosis.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [PROFESSION]. Diffuse right knee pain after knee to knee collision(s). 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is a moderate, diffuse bone contusion involving the most anterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle and a mild, small contusion at the most anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. There is a moderate focal bone contusion at the lateral aspect of the patella. No acute fracture on MRI. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
There is a moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is mild blunting/fraying of the inner margin of the medial meniscus without tear.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is partial thickness, in part delaminating cartilage fissuring (grade 3 chondral fissuring) at the central weightbearing aspect of the lateral femoral condyle (se 8, img 8 to 12). Very small marginal osteophytes.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is a chronic, 15 x 15 mm full-thickness cartilage defect (grade 4 chondral defect) at the groove of the femoral trochlea extending into the lateral aspect of the trochlea with subchondral cystic change. There is partial thickness cartilage fissuring (grade 2 chondral fissuring) at the medial and lateral patellar facets. 

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. There is a mild contusion/sprain of the joint capsule of the proximal tibiofibular joint.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: There is bony fragmentation of the tibial tubercle consistent with Osgood Schlatter Mild tendinosis and fraying and of the proximal and distal patellar tendon without tear . 
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 18 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:. 
1. Moderate, diffuse bone contusion involving the most anterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle and a mild, small contusion at the most anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. Additional moderate focal bone contusion at the lateral aspect of the patella.
2. Moderate joint effusion. 
3. Moderate chronic patellofemoral chondrosis and mild lateral compartment chondrosis. 
4. Mild contusion/sprain of the joint capsule of the proximal tibiofibular joint.
5. Osgood Schlatter with chronic tendinosis and fraying of both the proximal and distal patellar tendon without tendon tear. 
6. No meniscal or ligament tears.

Small suprapatellar effusion, a cluster of variably sized ossific loose bodies is appreciated posteromedially, the largest on measuring just over 1 cm across.

The medial meniscus appears intact.  
There is incomplete, chronic looking loss of lateral meniscal tissue throughout the corresponding posterior half, together with diffuse full-thickness chondral loss affecting the lateral tibial plateau.
No displaced meniscal fragments are present. 

Focal grade 3 chondral loss noted at the medial retropatellar facets, relatively mild age-related thinning of medial weightbearing hyaline cartilage.
There are nonetheless medial and lateral femorotibial marginal osteophytes.
Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus musculotendinous unit, distal iliotibial band and the patellar tendon.
Chronic looking calcific, quiescent distal insertional quadriceps tendinosis.
No fracture or marrow infiltration.
Grossly unremarkable imaged extra-articular soft tissues.
